page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. In the left margin, beside the line "dicentia", a small reference mark. No notes, no headings.

main_text.p: ente, certum interitum minatur. Hæc omnia sunt signa, quibus lethales febres & malignas ab aliis internoscimus. Cum igitur pestilentium febrium causæ, & symptomata ita satis hactenus explicata sint, superest ad earum curam progredi. Quapropter statim morbi initio corpus ægrotantis euacuare expedit. Verum unde euacuandum erit, diligenter consideret medicus oportet, ne naturæ motum auertat euacuatio. Quò enim natura uergit, eò ducere oportet per loca dicentia, quemadmodum ab Hippocrate, Aphorismo primo, & uicesimo Sectionis primæ, fideliter admonemur. Idcirco si eu[?] uomitu, aut cum alui profluuio pestiles febris incipiat, tum sanguis neutiquam mittendum erit, ne Naturam à suo munere auocemus, sed potius illam uomitoriis, aut pharmacis benignè purgantib. iuuabimus. Ea etenim, quæ per uiolentum uomitum humores nostri corporis cient, aut magno impetu p inferiora & superiora simul purgant, non paruum Naturæ nostræ facessunt negotium. Ideo tolerandi non sunt nostri temporis temerarij empyrici, alliciendi ad se pecuniam potius, quam morbum profligandi studio flagrantes, qui uel mercuria-

page.notes: Running head: the last word "NATVRÆ" is partly worn and marked [?]. Line 1 of the page is cut at the top, so the paragraph continues from the previous page (cont="true"). The text "dicentia" has a small mark over the "i" and a reference symbol in the left margin beside it; I could not read a letter or note text for it, so I did not write a note. "eu" in "Idcirco si eu uomitu" is hard to read and is marked [?]. "p inferiora" has a superscript mark over the p, possibly an abbreviation for per, copied as printed. Printed "uicefimo" has long s and is transcribed as "uicesimo". The word "symptomata" and "malignas" are split across lines without a visible hyphen, so they are written whole. Printed "sanguis" appears as "fanguis"; read as sanguis.
